notes.md: - **Unit sizes:** a **sar-i-khail** commanded **10 horsemen**; a sipah-salar commanded 10 sar-i-khails, and so on up to the khan (decimal system).
- **War elephants:** keeping elephants was a **privilege of the Sultan** alone; a **separate department** trained and maintained them.

new.s: In which year did Ibn Battuta arrive in India?
new.x: Ibn Battuta came to India in 1333, during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign, and stayed till 1342.
new.angle: U0109 notes gap: Ibn Battuta arrived 1333

new.s: Which post did Muhammad bin Tughlaq give to Ibn Battuta?
new.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq made Ibn Battuta the Qazi (judge) of Delhi.
new.angle: U0109 notes gap: Ibn Battuta office = Qazi of Delhi

new.s: Who is the author of Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi?
new.x: Ziauddin Barani wrote Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and Fatawa-i-Jahandari.
new.angle: U0109 notes gap: Barani -> Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi

new.s: Who founded the Bahmani kingdom in 1347?
new.x: Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu) founded the Bahmani kingdom in 1347 after a revolt against Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
new.angle: U0109 notes gap: Bahmani founder Hasan Gangu

new.s: Who is the author of Madhura Vijayam, which describes Tughlaq rule in the South?
new.x: Madhura Vijayam was written by Gangadevi; it describes the conditions under the Madurai Sultanate and Tughlaq rule.
new.angle: U0109 notes gap: Madhura Vijayam -> Gangadevi

new.s: Which of the following towns was founded by Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
new.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq founded Jaunpur, Firozabad, Fatehabad, Hisar Firoza and Firozpur.
new.angle: U0109 notes gap: Jaunpur founded by Firoz

new.s: Which kingdom was conquered by Bahlol Lodi?
new.x: Bahlol Lodi, founder of the Lodi dynasty, conquered the Sharqi kingdom of Jaunpur.
new.angle: U0110 notes gap: Bahlol Lodi conquered Jaunpur

new.s: Who was the last Sultan of Delhi?
new.x: Ibrahim Lodi was the last Delhi Sultan; he was killed by Babur at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.
new.angle: U0110 notes gap: last Delhi Sultan Ibrahim Lodi

new.s: Who built the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque at Delhi?
new.x: Qutbuddin Aibak, the first Sultan, built the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque and began the Qutub Minar.
new.angle: U0111 notes gap: Quwwat-ul-Islam -> Aibak

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Qutbuddin Aibak built the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque.
2. Iltutmish completed the Qutub Minar.
3. Alauddin Khalji built the top storey of the Qutub Minar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Aibak built the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque and began the Minar; Iltutmish completed it. Alauddin had no part in the Qutub Minar.
new.angle: U0111 notes gap: Quwwat-ul-Islam / Qutub Minar builders

new.s: Which Sultan of Delhi took the title Sikandar-i-Sani?
new.x: Alauddin Khalji called himself Sikandar-i-Sani, the Second Alexander.
new.angle: U0111 #6 notes gap: Sikandar-i-Sani -> Alauddin

new.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Title)
A. Lakh Baksh
B. Zil-i-Ilahi
C. Sikandar-i-Sani
D. Sultan-i-Azam
List-II (Ruler)
1. Alauddin Khalji
2. Qutbuddin Aibak
3. Iltutmish
4. Balban
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
new.x: Lakh Baksh = Aibak; Zil-i-Ilahi = Balban; Sikandar-i-Sani = Alauddin Khalji; Sultan-i-Azam = Iltutmish.
new.angle: U0111 #6 notes gap: titles -> Sultan (Sikandar-i-Sani)

new.s: In which year was the Second Battle of Tarain fought?
new.x: The Second Battle of Tarain (1192) opened North India to Turkish rule and led to the Delhi Sultanate.
new.angle: U0111 #7 notes gap: Second Tarain 1192

new.s: Whom did Muhammad Ghori defeat in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192)?
new.x: At Second Tarain in 1192 Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan; at Chandawar (1194) he defeated Jaichand.
new.angle: U0111 #7 notes gap: Second Tarain -> Ghori beat Prithviraj

new.s: Which dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate was called Kulah-Daran?
new.x: The Sayyids were called Kulah-Daran because they wore a pointed cap (kulah).
new.angle: U0111 notes gap: Kulah-Daran = Sayyids

new.s: Who is the author of Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh?
new.x: Badauni wrote Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh; he remarked on Muhammad bin Tughlaq's death.
new.angle: U0111 notes gap: Badauni -> Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh

new.s: Which of the following scholars was patronised by Qutbuddin Aibak?
new.x: Aibak patronised Hasan Nizami and Fakhr-i-Mudabbir.
new.angle: U0111 notes gap: Aibak patron of Hasan Nizami

new.s: Who among the following Sultans was called 'a slave of a slave'?
new.x: Iltutmish was a slave of Aibak, who was himself a slave of Muhammad Ghori; hence 'slave of a slave'.
new.angle: U0111 notes gap: Iltutmish slave of a slave

new.s: The poet Amir Khusrau is associated with the court of which of the following Sultans?
new.x: Amir Khusrau flourished in the reign of Alauddin Khalji.
new.angle: U0111 notes gap: Amir Khusrau in Alauddin's reign

new.s: Who founded the Sharqi kingdom of Jaunpur?
new.x: Khwaja Jahan founded the Sharqi kingdom of Jaunpur under the last Tughlaq; Bahlol Lodi annexed it in 1476.
new.angle: U0111 #9 notes gap: Jaunpur Sharqi founder Khwaja Jahan

new.s: How many times did the Delhi Sultanate invade Andhra between 1303 and 1323?
new.x: Delhi invaded Andhra five times between 1303 and 1323; in 1323 Ulugh Khan captured Prataparudra II.
new.angle: U0111 #9 notes gap: Andhra invaded five times 1303-1323

new.s: Which department of the Delhi Sultanate dealt with finance and revenue?
new.x: The Diwan-i-Wizarat, headed by the Wazir, handled finance and revenue.
new.angle: U0112 #2 notes gap: Diwan-i-Wizarat = finance

new.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, the Chief Sadr (Sadr-us-Sudur) also held which office?
new.x: The Chief Sadr, head of religious affairs, was usually also the Chief Qazi.
new.angle: U0112 notes gap: Chief Sadr also Chief Qazi

new.s: What was the real name of Balban?
new.x: Balban's real name was Baha-ud-din; he got the title Ulugh Khan from Nasiruddin Mahmud.
new.angle: U0112 notes gap: Balban's real name Baha-ud-din

new.s: Which Sultan introduced the court customs of sijda and paibos?
new.x: Balban introduced sijda (prostration) and paibos (kissing the Sultan's feet) and the Persian festival Nauroz.
new.angle: U0112 #11 notes gap: sijda, paibos -> Balban

new.s: Which ruler issued gold coins with the figure of Goddess Lakshmi?
new.x: Muhammad Ghori issued coins with Goddess Lakshmi; Mahmud of Ghazni's silver coins carried Arabic and Devanagari Sanskrit.
new.angle: U0112 notes gap: Ghori coins with Lakshmi

new.s: Which system was used to bring fruits of Khorasan to Delhi?
new.x: The ulaq, the horse post, brought Khorasan fruit to Delhi; the dawa was the foot post.
new.angle: U0113 #7 notes gap: Ulaq brought Khorasan fruit

new.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, to whom was inam land granted?
new.x: Inam was land granted to religious men; jagir went to mansabdars and amaram to Amaranayakas.
new.angle: U0113 #2 notes gap: inam = grants to religious men

new.s: In the Sultanate army, how many horsemen did a sar-i-khail command?
new.x: A sar-i-khail, the lowest commander, led 10 horsemen; each higher rank commanded 10 of the rank below.
new.angle: U0113 web: #5 army ranks -> unit sizes

new.s: Who among the following could keep war elephants in the Delhi Sultanate?
new.x: Keeping elephants was a royal privilege of the Sultan; a separate department trained and maintained them.
new.angle: U0113 web: #8 war elephants -> royal monopoly

new.s: Who paid kharaj in the Delhi Sultanate?
new.x: Kharaj was the land tax, usually one-third of the produce, paid by non-Muslim cultivators; Muslims paid ushr.
new.angle: U0114 #1 notes gap: kharaj -> payer

new.s: What was jizya in the Delhi Sultanate?
new.x: Jizya was a poll tax paid by non-Muslims; Firoz extended it to Brahmins.
new.angle: U0114 #1 notes gap: jizya = poll tax

new.s: What was 'khams' in the Delhi Sultanate?
o: The State's one-fifth share of war booty
new.x: Khams was the State's share of war booty, one-fifth; the rest went to the soldiers.
new.angle: U0114 #1 notes gap: khams = 1/5 of booty (APPSC 2012)

new.s: What was 'ghari', a cess introduced by Alauddin Khalji?
new.x: Ghari was a house tax and charai a grazing tax, both first charged by Alauddin Khalji.
new.angle: U0114 #5 notes gap: ghari = house tax

new.s: What was the land tax of the Kakatiyas called?
new.x: The Kakatiya land tax was Ari; Maagani was irrigated land and Metta rain-fed land.
new.angle: U0114 notes gap: Kakatiya land tax Ari

new.s: Who introduced the silver tanka and the copper jital?
new.x: Iltutmish introduced the silver tanka and copper jital, the first regular standard currency of the Sultanate.
new.angle: U0114 #3 notes gap: tanka, jital -> Iltutmish (APPSC 2018)
